subsystems.name: Quantum processor
subsystems.role: the physical qubits that store and manipulate the quantum state of the simulated electrons.

subsystems.name: Control and readout
subsystems.role: drives qubit operations and reads out the final state.

subsystems.name: Error correction
subsystems.role: combines many noisy physical qubits into a smaller number of reliable logical qubits.

subsystems.name: Algorithm and compilation
subsystems.role: translates the molecular problem into a sequence of quantum gates.

subsystems.name: Classical co-processor
subsystems.role: prepares inputs, runs outer-loop optimisations and analyses results.

subsystems.name: Software stack
subsystems.role: programming languages, libraries and workflows that tie the layers together.

buildSteps.title: Define the chemistry problem
buildSteps.detail: Choose a molecule or material and select an active space of orbitals and electrons that captures the important correlation.

buildSteps.title: Map electrons to qubits
buildSteps.detail: Encode the fermionic Hamiltonian as a sum of Pauli operators using a transformation such as Jordan-Wigner or Bravyi-Kitaev.

buildSteps.title: Design the quantum circuit
buildSteps.detail: Select an algorithm — variational eigensolver for near-term devices or quantum phase estimation for fault-tolerant ones — and compile it into native gates.

buildSteps.title: Prepare the quantum state
buildSteps.detail: Initialise the qubits in a reference state, often a Hartree-Fock solution, then apply the circuit to create the correlated state.

buildSteps.title: Protect against errors
buildSteps.detail: Either run error mitigation on noisy hardware or encode logical qubits in an error-correcting code and repeatedly measure syndromes to detect and correct faults.

buildSteps.title: Execute and measure
buildSteps.detail: Run the circuit many times and measure qubits in different bases to estimate the expectation values of the Hamiltonian terms.

buildSteps.title: Post-process classically
buildSteps.detail: Combine measurements to obtain the ground-state energy and other properties, and iterate if using a variational loop.

buildSteps.title: Validate and scale
buildSteps.detail: Compare against exact classical results for small systems, then increase the active space and qubit count toward chemically relevant accuracy.

prerequisites.why: small error-correcting codes have been demonstrated, but millions of physical qubits may be needed for useful chemistry.
Hamiltonian simulation, phase estimation and variational methods are well developed in theory.
gate errors must be low enough that error correction can succeed at scale.
methods like density functional theory and coupled cluster provide reference energies and guide active-space selection.
chemists and materials scientists must identify problems where classical methods fail and quantum simulation can help.

pathway.milestone: small-molecule demonstrations on noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices
early fault-tolerant devices with tens to hundreds of logical qubits
pathway.unlocks: quantum advantage for small strongly correlated systems beyond exact classical simulation.

pathway.milestone: application-specific advantage for catalysts, battery electrolytes or drug fragments
pathway.unlocks: real design problems where quantum simulation changes industrial decisions.

pathway.milestone: routine quantum chemistry integrated into materials and pharmaceutical discovery
pathway.unlocks: faster, cheaper development of new catalysts, batteries and medicines.
